BiblicalUsage: Cheres is a word with two faces, the sun and the itch, and both show up in its few appearances. In Deuteronomy it is the itch of Egypt laid on the disobedient, in Job it is the sun God commands not to rise, and in Judges it marks the time before the sun was up and before the sun went down.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a single word can carry both judgment and the turning of the day, and that is how rich the language of Scripture is. I believe God writes both meanings into one word on purpose, so that I remember His judgments and His mercies come from the same hand.
